title: Manuel Perez's mute use, plunger origins and the coconut shell
summary: Perez used mutes on waltzes; the plunger was a Chicago-era thing like the tin can, and Dominique never saw a coconut shell used.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: Did Manuel Perez ever use any of those nukes and things like that?
Yeah. Manuel used a nukes. And you know he used to use the nukes on waltzes.
Well, you left your plunger out.
Yeah. Did they use that plunger back in New Orleans too? Is that something that worked here later? No. It's something that worked here.
Worked up here. See that plunger? Same thing as taking a can. Yeah. Same thing. They do that with the tin can? Tin can. We used to do it with the tin can.
Did you ever see anybody do it with the coconut shell? No, never did.
I never see anyone do it with the coconut shell. No. They're not telling you that story.
Use it like a plunger. Hold out half of the coconut shell.
Yeah. Well, how it sounds like that?
Pretty good. Pretty good, eh? Yeah.
Never heard of that. He must be heard I couldn't buy a plunger. I don't know.
